image.subject: two burnt-down candles on a bare oak writing desk in a Restoration-era study at dusk, a steel-nib pen laid down across an open leather writing case, 1830s Paris

storyboard.claim: Knowing when to stop writing is the hardest part of authorship.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Burnt-down candles and a pen laid down on a bare desk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the closing section after the Villefort and Danglars audit.
storyboard.addedInformation: The desk is empty: the work is finished.

image.subject: a small two-masted Mediterranean ship with full pale sails sailing away from a rocky island at dusk, seen from the shore, indigo sea, 1830s

storyboard.claim: The story ends with a ship sailing away.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A two-masted ship with pale sails heads out to sea from a rocky island.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Cuts from the desk to the sea.
storyboard.addedInformation: The ship leaves Monte Cristo island behind.

image.subject: a grave young officer in a dark blue naval coat with brass buttons, fair short hair, pale worried face, standing on a rocky Mediterranean shore beside a pale-dressed young woman, watching a distant ship, 1830s

storyboard.claim: Morrel and Valentine are left behind on the island.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Morrel in his blue naval coat beside Valentine on rocks, looking out to sea.
storyboard.addedInformation: The two young lovers are stranded on the island.

image.subject: a folded sealed letter lying on a rough stone ledge inside a dim sea grotto, a single candle beside it, damp rock walls, 1830s

storyboard.claim: They find a final letter.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A sealed letter on a stone ledge in a grotto.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Morrel and Valentine turn from the sea.
storyboard.addedInformation: The letter holds the count's philosophy.

storyboard.claim: True authorship means knowing when to stop writing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only quotation card.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the book's closing lesson in plain words.

image.subject: a closed ledger bound in green leather lying on a bare wooden table in a sunlit room, 1830s Paris

storyboard.claim: Stopping is a transition from active destruction to the sea.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A closed ledger on a table, sealed away.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Quote gives way to the ledger image.
storyboard.addedInformation: The ledger stands for the finished vengeance.

image.subject: an old hand-drawn map of the Mediterranean coast with brass dividers resting across Marseille and the islands, candlelit table, 1830s

storyboard.claim: The story moves from Paris back to the sea.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An old map with brass dividers across the Mediterranean.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: After the ledger, the map shows the move.
storyboard.addedInformation: Dividers measure distance from Paris to the Mediterranean.

storyboard.claim: Dantès spent fourteen passive years in the Château d'If.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only timeline of years.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets up the contrast with the active years.
storyboard.addedInformation: The passive years are the prison years.

storyboard.claim: Later years were spent calculated and active.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only stat card.
storyboard.addedInformation: The years of revenge follow the prison years.

image.subject: a lamp-lit Paris counting-house with rows of bound ledgers on shelves and a clerk's high desk, 1830s

storyboard.claim: He ran a corporation of revenge in Paris.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Rows of ledgers in a lamp-lit Paris office.
storyboard.addedInformation: The office stands for the revenge machine.

image.subject: Edmond Dantès as the Count of Monte Cristo: a tall pale aristocrat in his thirties in a black frock coat and white silk cravat, dark hair swept back, leaving a Paris townhouse at dawn with a travel trunk, 1830s

storyboard.claim: He leaves Paris and the remaining millions behind.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The count steps out of a Paris townhouse with a travel trunk.
storyboard.addedInformation: The count abandons his fortune.

storyboard.claim: Is the departure a triumphant victory lap?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only question card.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Raises the common reading of the departure.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets up the argument against it.

storyboard.claim: He audited, balanced, rewarded and bankrupted.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only list of four actions.
storyboard.addedInformation: The four verbs are the case for victory.

image.subject: a signed bond certificate lying on a banker's mahogany desk beside a small stack of gold coins, 1830s Paris bond exchange

storyboard.claim: He beat the financial system and can retire.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A bond certificate and gold coins on a banker's desk.
storyboard.addedInformation: The bond certificate is the instrument he mastered.

image.subject: a sailing ship's white wake fading at sunset, a rocky island receding on the horizon of a calm Mediterranean sea, 1830s

storyboard.claim: The departure is melancholy, not a celebration.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A ship's wake fading at sunset beside a receding island.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the victory reading to the melancholy reading.
storyboard.addedInformation: The sunset makes the departure feel final.

image.subject: Edmond Dantès as the Count of Monte Cristo: a tall pale aristocrat in his thirties in a black frock coat and white silk cravat, dark hair swept back, standing alone at a ship's rail with his hands on the wood, looking back at the island, 1830s

storyboard.claim: The departure is an exhausted surrender.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The count alone at the ship's rail looking back.
storyboard.addedInformation: He looks back at what he gave up.

image.subject: a hand of playing cards fanned face-down on a dark green card table in candlelight, one card turned over to show a crown, 1830s

storyboard.claim: He holds all the cards but has lost his soul.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Fanned cards on a green table.
storyboard.addedInformation: The game is the cost of his soul.

image.subject: an empty carved oak chair standing alone in a dim stone hall, a single candle on the floor beside it, 1830s

storyboard.claim: He abdicates the throne he built.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An empty carved chair in a dim hall.
storyboard.addedInformation: The chair is his self-made throne, now abandoned.

image.subject: a black ink stain spreading across the white linen cuff of a man's shirt, candlelight, 1830s

storyboard.claim: Justice written with the pen leaves ink on your hands.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An ink stain on a white cuff.
storyboard.addedInformation: The stain is the collateral damage.

image.subject: a stack of sealed letters tied with string on a dark wooden desk, unopened, candle beside them, 1830s

storyboard.claim: The consequences were unintended and must be held to account.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sealed letters tied with string.
storyboard.addedInformation: Each sealed letter is a consequence he did not weigh.

image.subject: a black judicial robe draped over a wooden chair in a candlelit study beside a plain white wall, 1830s

storyboard.claim: He appoints himself both judge and deity.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A black judicial robe over a chair.
storyboard.addedInformation: The robe stands for self-appointed judgement.

image.subject: a pair of brass scales sitting perfectly level on a wooden counter with nothing on either pan, 1830s counting-house

storyboard.claim: He believes his ledger is perfectly balanced.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Level brass scales on a counter.
storyboard.addedInformation: The level scale is his self-assessment.

image.subject: an open ledger page on a candlelit desk with a red ink stain spreading across its columns, 1830s

storyboard.claim: The books are balanced with innocent blood.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A ledger page with a red ink stain spreading.
storyboard.addedInformation: The red stain is the innocent cost.

storyboard.claim: Like little Edward, Villefort's young son?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only question card.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the child caught in the audits.

image.subject: a small brown glass poison bottle standing beside a porcelain teacup on a dim Paris salon table, 1830s

storyboard.claim: His mother poisons the boy, pushed by the count's pressure.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A small poison bottle beside a teacup.
storyboard.addedInformation: The poison is the mechanism, not a person.

image.subject: a folded black mourning shawl draped over a chair beside a tall window in a dim Paris room, 1830s

storyboard.claim: The mother is pushed to wipe out her own bloodline.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A folded black mourning shawl over a chair.
storyboard.addedInformation: The shawl signals the loss.

image.subject: a young pale dark-haired woman in a white nightdress lying still with closed eyes on a white bed under soft lamplight, 1830s bedchamber, peaceful

storyboard.claim: Valentine is put through psychological torture and forced into a death-like sleep.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A young woman lying still on a white bed.
storyboard.addedInformation: The sleep is engineered, not a death.

image.subject: a small white child's shoe resting alone on a worn stone doorstep at dawn, 1830s Paris

storyboard.claim: Children pay the compound interest on their parents' debts.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A small white shoe on a stone step.
storyboard.addedInformation: The shoe stands for the innocent child.

image.subject: an empty dusty Paris street at dawn with a single lit window in a grey stone building, 1830s

storyboard.claim: The debts date back to 1815.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An empty Paris street at dawn with one lit window.
storyboard.addedInformation: The street is the aftermath of the old betrayal.

image.subject: a man's face half in shadow reflected in a tall gilt-framed mirror in a candlelit Paris room, 1830s

storyboard.claim: He became the man he hated.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A reflected face half in shadow in a gilt mirror.
storyboard.addedInformation: The mirror shows the reversal.

image.subject: a child's wooden toy soldier lying on a dark wooden floor beside a candle that has fallen over, 1830s

storyboard.claim: Seeing the child's death breaks the mechanism of vengeance.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A toy soldier on the floor beside a fallen candle.
storyboard.addedInformation: The toy stands for the child's loss, no body shown.

image.subject: a red wax seal being pressed onto a folded letter on a dark desk, a brass signet ring in hand, 1830s

storyboard.claim: He realises he has gone too far.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A wax seal pressed onto a letter.
storyboard.addedInformation: The seal closes the account.

storyboard.claim: The web unpacked: dungeon capital, bond shorting, poison.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only list of three threads.
storyboard.addedInformation: Three threads of the web.

image.subject: a heavy iron-bound chest standing open on a stone floor with gold coins spilling from it, 1830s

storyboard.claim: He did not just escape a prison; he bought the world.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An open iron-bound chest of gold coins.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the summary of the web.
storyboard.addedInformation: The chest is his fortune.

image.subject: a large iron key turning in the lock of a heavy oak door of a Paris townhouse, 1830s

storyboard.claim: He foreclosed on the men's fates.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An iron key in a heavy oak door lock.
storyboard.addedInformation: The key is the act of foreclosure.

image.subject: an open ledger page with its columns balanced in neat ink, a quill resting beside it on a wooden desk, 1830s

storyboard.claim: Revenge was a spiritual ledger being balanced.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An open ledger with balanced columns and a quill.
storyboard.addedInformation: Revenge reframed as accounting.

storyboard.claim: Time and wealth eventually collect the debt.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only quotation card.
storyboard.addedInformation: Restates the thesis.

image.subject: an hourglass standing on a stone windowsill with warm sunlight falling across it, 1830s

storyboard.claim: His final command is wait and hope.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An hourglass on a sunlit stone windowsill.
storyboard.addedInformation: The hourglass is the latency period.

storyboard.claim: What debts in your own life are still waiting to be collected?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only closing question.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the chunk and the book.
storyboard.addedInformation: Turns the question to the viewer.
